name: animated-frameworks

frames.best_why: The middle Next.js tile sits slightly raised and larger than its neighbours mid-lift.

tagline: Three framework tiles tilt up in turn above a softly pulsing circuit line.
summary: A compatibility card with React, Next.js and HTML5 tiles that lift and tilt in 3D one after another. A faint circuit path behind them carries a travelling blue pulse, with a heading and blurb underneath.
appearance: A tall dark card holding three rounded square tiles in a row, each with a small white framework glyph, over a faint corner-to-corner circuit line. A heading and two lines of grey text sit at the bottom.
behaviour: The tiles take turns lifting, tilting back and moving toward the viewer over a slow cycle, while a soft blue glow travels along the circuit path behind them. The text stays still.
demo_content: Heading Universal Compatibility with a line saying it works with React, Next.js and plain HTML.
search_phrases: compatibility card with react next html
tiles that pop up one at a time
works with any framework feature card
integration logo card for landing page
use_when: A devtool landing page needs a compact card that names the frameworks or stacks it supports.
avoid_when: The three tiles and their icons are fixed, so showing other tools means editing the component, and the lift is tiny.
customise: The heading and description are props. The three framework tiles, their icons, the colours and the looping timing are fixed in the source.
weight_why: Three tiles with CSS transforms, one SVG pulse and a chain of timers; no per-frame JS.

a11y.note: The looping lift and pulse ignore reduced-motion, and the framework icons have no text alternative beyond the description.

props.name: cardDescription
props.default: "Works seamlessly with React, Next.js, plain HTML and more.

issues: The travelling circuit pulse is so faint on the dark card that it barely reads.
The 3D lift is only a few pixels, so the stills look almost identical.
polish_why: Neat three-tile card, but the lift and pulse are too faint to notice and it never stops.
title: Animated Frameworks
